summary: Round-4 verification of a decomposition commit (no code). Every factual claim added this round was checked against source and all of them hold. P13/P10: the mechanism prescriptions really are gone and what replaced them is accurate -- ChainEntry.java:50 does record the reserved kind as consumed ('CLAIMED BY ADR-0032, on exactly the terms this comment reserved it'), ADR-0028:130 really does leave the version path open ('Foreclosed: nothing. A fifth version can add fields to the kinded layout, and v0 keeps parsing regardless'), Checkpoint.java:151 really does compare against one constant, CheckpointCursor.newest (CheckpointCursor.java:72-81) really does let decode's IOException out, BinStore.java:32-36 really does define IOException as 'the store is unreachable', and the M3.0 quotation is verbatim at backlog-done.md:93. Nothing dangles: no surviving reference to chain-delta-v2.bin or golden/checkpoint-v1.bin anywhere in the tree. The one thing the deletion dropped -- 'leaving VERSION = 0 over changed bytes makes an OLDER READER parse a qualified key as a bare podId' -- is still covered, because 'Choose each discriminator in the ADR' requires the Checkpoint to have one at all; I do not raise it. P11: the both-tiers wording matches GoldenCheckpointTest's javadoc lines 24-34 exactly (delete-the-sort green in all three; Map.copyOf fails theGoldenBytesCarryStreamsAndPodsInASCENDINGOrder 6 of 6), and CheckpointTest really holds the two named order detectors. T5: verified -- CheckpointWriterContentTest:143-145 constructs the takeover fixture with everyDeltas=1 and asserts poda->42 in a written checkpoint before the takeover, and CheckpointWriter.java:157 makes 'a commit after the last checkpoint' genuinely unsatisfiable at that setting. T7: verified against .harness/review/acf50ad67afe -- reviewer 5 findings of which 3 major, test-reviewer 6 of which 3 major: eleven and six, exact. P12 (my own round-3 finding): the rendering is right on the half it states -- pods.merge in CheckpointWriter.java:124-129 has no eviction, a recovered fold would union the predecessor's entries, and ADR-0033's Context rejects 'an object that grows with history' in those words -- but its other half, 'widening the value instead stays O(pods)', is falsified by the T4 paragraph added to M4.10d in the same commit. That is P15 below. And the T4 fix deleted only one of the two copies of the claim it was deleting: P14.

findings.title: The 'M4.10d does not depend on M4.10c' claim was deleted from the notes and left standing in the authoritative table, in the same commit
findings.failure_scenario: backlog-notes.md:186 now says 'M4.10d is blocked by M4.10b, and DEPENDS on M4.10c's outcome', and backlog-notes.md:313-318 spells out why ('An earlier draft of the parent row claimed M4.10d survives M4.10c's outcome either way. It does not.'). The parent row in backlog.md -- added by this same staged diff, and the file AGENTS.md calls 'the current task list, authoritative' -- still ends 'd is the dedup and is blocked by b, not by c.' Both files are staged; the commit asserts the dependency and denies it. Concretely: next-task loads backlog.md's open rows, not backlog-notes.md, and it is the rows that say what is blocked. A session finishing M4.10b reads row M4.10 ('c is conditional on that answer and may be void; d is ... blocked by b, not by c') and row M4.10d ('Blocked by M4.10b.'), concludes d is unblocked while c is still open, and starts the dedup. It then hits the case the notes just added -- a replay whose original commit is behind the newest checkpoint -- with no format able to carry the answer, and either stalls or ships the current-offsets mutation that backlog-notes.md:305-311 names as the parent row's own harm arriving through the fix for it. This is the failure the tree's own record names twice in its own words: backlog-notes.md:174 (M4.8) 'BOTH COPIES OF A SPLIT MUST SAY SO ... the one-copy-fixed failure', and baselines/review.txt's rounds:M4.10a entry 'AND DELETING THE SECTION MISSED ITS DUPLICATE: the same facts sat inside the M4.10 row'. The fix is one clause in the row; M4.10d's own row saying only 'Blocked by M4.10b' should follow it.

findings.title: 'The original offsets are unrecoverable ... which a recovered window must therefore carry' is false as stated, and directs per-commit run offsets into the checkpoint -- the size axis ADR-0033 exists to hold, and the one the sibling paragraph claims stays O(pods)
findings.failure_scenario: The new paragraph reasons: Checkpoint.pods is Map<String, Long>, so once the original commit is behind the newest checkpoint 'the original offsets are unrecoverable', therefore (backlog-notes.md:186) 'a replay must return the original offsets, which a recovered window must therefore carry'. The premise does not hold. The offsets are in the delta and are absolute -- RunCommit.java:19 is 'record RunCommit(RunKey key, int recordCount, long firstOffset)' -- and that delta is addressable without a search, because LogKeys.java:34 is 'String keyFor(long sequence)' over (prefix, epoch, sequence). So a checkpoint that carries per pod a two-long (epoch, sequence) pointer alongside the flushSeq answers a replay with ONE get at a derived key, no scan, no list, and no growth: that is exactly ADR-0033's own division of labour, 'It does not carry the offset-to-segment index, which stays in the deltas'. Taken as written, the row instead tells M4.10c to put the offsets themselves in the recovered window, i.e. per pod, the (RunKey, firstOffset) of every run in that pod's last commit. Sizing that: the existing streams map is bounded by streams and is what ADR-0033 sizes at 'tens of kilobytes' and asserts 'under 64 KiB at 1,600 streams'; the new field is bounded by the number of (pod, stream) pairs flushed in one window, which is a second copy of that map at best and pods x streams at worst -- Sequencer.java:74-76 states plainly that 'two nodes may commit the same stream in one batch window', and ADR-0017 is 'every pod writes'. At 300 plugin nodes that is a checkpoint two to three orders of magnitude over the bound the ADR asserts, re-PUT on every checkpoint tick and decoded on every recovery and by every M5 tier-3 reader. The row therefore carries a size hazard larger than the one it flags one section earlier, while asserting at backlog-notes.md:231-232 that 'Widening the value instead stays O(pods)' -- which is true of (qualifier, flushSeq) and false of (qualifier, flushSeq, all of the last commit's run offsets). Compounding it: neither M4.10b's section (backlog-notes.md:191-215, whose output is 'A LIST OF FORMATS' and which weighs only the key) nor M4.10c's section says anything about answering a replay, and M4.10c is the ONLY commit allowed to change the format -- the split's own banner at backlog-notes.md:178-181 says a format change 'cannot be a hunk inside a larger commit'. So even read charitably as 'be able to produce the offsets', the requirement is stated in the one row that cannot act on it. What the row should say is the property, not the payload: a replay must return the ORIGINAL offsets, so M4.10b must decide what the checkpoint carries to reach them, and whatever it chooses must leave the checkpoint bounded by pods and streams rather than by the runs of a commit.

findings.title: Two inserted sentences are joined onto the end of the preceding paragraph, so a new cost constraint renders mid-paragraph where every other one is a ⚠️ heading
findings.failure_scenario: Every other warning in this file begins a paragraph, which is what makes the file skimmable under the progressive-disclosure rule AGENTS.md states -- a session reads the ⚠️ blocks of the one section it picked. Two of this round's inserts do not: line 228 puts '⚠️ AND QUALIFY THE VALUE, NOT THE KEY' at the end of the line beginning 'failure this task exists to prevent, reintroduced by the fix for it.', and line 264 trails 'Deleting that assertion instead is the testing.md rule 5 inversion' onto 'so the fixture must change that setting.' In rendered markdown both are mid-paragraph. The consequence is small but real and is on the cost constraint specifically: a session picking M4.10c and scanning the ⚠️ headings of its section sees THE TWO FORMATS DISCRIMINATE DIFFERENTLY, OLD OBJECTS MUST STILL DECODE, FORMAT-LEVEL CRITERIA ARE NOT ENOUGH and THE GOLDEN MUST DISCRIMINATE -- and not the one paragraph that bounds the checkpoint's size. A blank line before each is the whole fix; per review.md a minor need not be fixed at all.
